pointers.sentence: Each layer is called with a request, may do some work, calls the layer inside it, may do more work on the response that comes back, and returns it (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

A middleware that reads on the way in something another one puts on the request has to come after it in the list: `AuthenticationMiddleware` refuses to run unless the session middleware has already set the session on the request (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:AuthenticationMiddleware.process_request`).

The `process_request` hooks run outermost first and the `process_response` hooks innermost first, yet the handler calls neither: `MiddlewareMixin`, the base class nearly all of Django's middleware use, calls them when its layer is called, one before it calls the layer inside and the other on what comes back ([Building the middleware chain](handlers/chain.md)) (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__call__`).
The `process_view` hooks and the view are called from the centre ([The centre of the chain](handlers/view.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

And the request ends after the handler has returned: the server closes the response, and closing it sends `request_finished` ([The two entry points](handlers/entry.md#who-ends-the-request)) (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.close`).

Most of Django's own middleware are synchronous only, so they run together on a thread of the request's own while the centre runs on the event loop, and each change of mode is a crossing between the loop and a thread ([Sync and async in one chain](handlers/async.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).
[How an exception becomes a response](handlers/exceptions.md) has the whole table, and says what does get through (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`).
